_note: Thresholds for tool/analyze_audio.py. A stem is judged on what is true of the stem; a mix is judged on integrated LUFS, which is a programme measure and only means something once the layers are summed. A missing key means the limit is ON, not off.

stem._mono_ok_note: Sub beds are meant to be mono. A low layer that is wide only smears the centre image and costs headroom. Naming them here says the same thing as saying it in the patch.

mix._window_note: Ten decibels of loudness change from open air to the bottom of the world is the design. The floor is -26 so a profile has headroom at the quiet end instead of sitting exactly on the line, which is what made the first pass fail by 0.1 dB. A profile 20 dB under the floor still fails.

_share_floor_note: Two thresholds, because they are different claims. Below -40 dB a layer is off: that is a defect and it fails the build. Between -40 and the advisory line it may be a deliberate whisper, which is a decision for the ear, so it is reported and not failed. The advisory line is mix_layer_share_advisory_db.

open_findings.why: 0.00208 against a 0.002 limit. Subtracting 0.5 from every saw voice was tried and made it far worse (DC -0.71), so the saws are already zero-mean and the offset comes from somewhere else in the chain.
-0.94 dBFS against a -1.0 limit. Marginal, and the mix trim already sits far below it, so it is a measurement-honesty item rather than something audible.

resolved_findings.how: The stereo difference has to exist before the first filter, be built from bare sources with different seeds, be wrapped in stereo(), and be handed to a single out() argument. out(field |> lp(...) |> hp(...)) gives correlation 0.00 where the old out(x.pan(0.15), x.pan(-0.15)) gave 1.000.
Same rule. The sub undertone is added afterwards as its own stereo pair so the bandpass cannot swallow it.
